question: Does an exhaustive balanced partition of the 18 public NCSX coils into three equal winding circuits reduce both worst single-circuit-loss magnetic-shape departure and distributed-force departure relative to a type-segregated three-circuit control, without a force overshoot or numerical-instability failure?
assumptions: This is a new-design winding-partition screen on public NCSX geometry, not a reconstruction or retrofit recommendation for the historical NCSX electrical system.
Each candidate circuit contains two copies of each of the three coil types; type-dependent turn count realizes the declared nominal ampere-turns under a common series current.

The declared fault endpoint sets one complete circuit current to zero while the other two remain nominal. Twenty-one proportional intermediate states audit the path but do not solve an electrical or thermal transient.

Magnetic departure is the RMS surface-normal field left after removing the best common-current scaling. Force departure is the length-weighted RMS change from the corresponding common-current-squared distributed-force pattern.
The comparator places all six symmetry copies of one coil type in each circuit. It is a conceptual equal-count control, not a claim about historical NCSX wiring or an industry standard.
The reference mesh selects the candidate exhaustively; the fine mesh checks the frozen candidate without reselection.
Thresholds were fixed during interactive reference-grid exploration rather than preregistered before every reference result was observed, so this is exploratory evidence.

Passing justifies a coupled circuit, quench, voltage, thermal, and structural feasibility model. It does not establish a practical circuit, safe plasma survival, novelty, patentability, or commercial value.

requirements.statement: The fine-grid candidate reduces worst single-circuit-loss magnetic-shape departure by at least 1.25 times relative to the type-segregated control.
The fine-grid candidate reduces worst single-circuit-loss distributed-force departure by at least 1.1 times relative to the type-segregated control.
No sampled partial-loss state exceeds the nominal peak local inter-coil force density.
The sampled partial-loss path has no magnetic or force-departure overshoot greater than one percent beyond its complete-loss endpoint.
The worse of the magnetic and force reduction-factor changes is no more than two percent between reference and fine meshes.
Symmetry-related candidate circuits have no more than one-billionth relative spread in fine-grid magnetic or force departure.

categorical_requirements.statement: The selected architecture partitions all 18 physical coils exactly once and places two copies of every coil type in each circuit.
